name: load_debug_symbol_tables
note: reads two counted tables from g_object_output (00447f24, opened "rb", see globals): u16 LE count, then per entry a length byte + that many bytes. Table 1 -> 0x20-byte debug_symbol nodes (FUN_0040cf00(0x20)): +6 = kind*2|1, +4 id, +7 location type (6 = stack offset, 4 bytes, a negative one is rebased by the frame size from FUN_0042ec79 and the 0x44-byte frame table DAT_0044bc74 of the current function DAT_0044e148; otherwise 1 byte = register), kind 0xe gets an 8-byte attachment at +0x1c; chained into g_debug_symbol_hash (0x7f buckets by id). Table 2 -> 0xc-byte debug_location nodes into g_debug_location_hash. Errors 0xce6 (read). Callers FUN_0040f97b (tag 0x32 scope 3), FUN_0041080f (tag 0x34, which builds the same nodes) guard it with DAT_00447cb4. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused by callers)

name: free_debug_symbol_table
note: frees every 0x20-byte node of g_debug_symbol_hash (and its 8-byte attachment at +0x1c) with FUN_0040d5cb, clears the 0x7f buckets, then frees the 0x104-byte string pool blocks (g_string_pool_blocks) and resets g_string_pool_pos/end. Callers FUN_0040f97b (scope end)

name: free_debug_location_table
note: frees the 0xc-byte nodes of g_debug_location_hash (0x7f buckets) and clears the buckets; called with free_debug_symbol_table at scope end (FUN_0040f97b)

name: store_string_in_pool
note: copies len bytes + NUL into the string pool (0x104-byte blocks = next pointer + 0x100 bytes, chained in g_string_pool_blocks, allocated with FUN_0040cf00 when the rest of the block is too small); returns the copy, NULL for len 0. Caller FUN_0041080f stores it as the debug symbol's name (+0x18)

name: emit_import_symbol
note: looks the symbol up (FUN_00427a7d); unless it is kind 10 with misc != 0xff: if its name is a runtime routine (g_runtime_routine_names 1..0xb6) sets the routine's bit in g_runtime_routines_imported and records the import index in g_runtime_routine_import_index; unless symbol flag 0x40: object mode (request +0x12 == 1) writes an import record (tag 0xc: 0xc0, name length+1, '_', name; tag 0x8c to force a new record when the buffer is short) and gives the symbol import number g_import_symbol_index++ at +0x28; listing mode prints ".IMPORT _name" (s__IMPORT_0043c034). Callers run_assembler_passes (kind 10/11 symbols), emit_runtime_routine_imports

name: emit_runtime_routine_imports
note: for each bit of g_runtime_routines_used (32 bytes, MSB first, routine = bit+1) creates the routine's symbol (FUN_00416e00(0xb,0x80,id), name from g_runtime_routine_names) and imports it with emit_import_symbol unless g_runtime_routines_imported already has it (then copies the saved import index to +0x28). Caller run_assembler_passes

name: emit_export_symbol
note: unless kind 7..9 with misc != 0xff: object mode writes an export record (tag 0x14: kind-dependent word/flag, section number from +0x1a, big-endian address from +8, name with '_' prefix; tag 0x94 to force a new record) and numbers the symbol with g_export_symbol_index++ at +0x28; listing mode prints ".EXPORT _name" (s__EXPORT_0043c03c). Caller run_assembler_passes (kinds 7,8,9,0xc with flag 0x80)

name: build_section_select_record
note: object mode only: writes 0x9a, 7, a zero word and the big-endian section number of the current section kind (g_current_section_kind 0..3 -> DAT_0044e028/2a/2c/2e) at out, clears g_section_data_bytes, returns 6 (bytes written); 0 in listing mode. Caller append_object_record_bytes before a data record (tags 0x1c/0x9c) when g_object_need_section_select is set; the caller then closes it as record 0x1a

name: count_import_and_export_symbols
note: walks the symbol table (DAT_0044e14c, request +0xac entries of 0x2c bytes): an exported (flag 0x80) kind 7..9 symbol with misc != 0xff decrements g_export_symbol_count (it will not be exported, see emit_export_symbol); kind 11, or kind 10 with misc == 0xff, without flag 0x40 counts in g_import_symbol_count and marks its runtime routine in a local bitmap; then counts the routines of g_runtime_routines_used not marked. Both counts go to the object header (FUN_00412b7c) and request +0xe4/+0xe8 (store_request_record_updates). Caller run_assembler_passes

name: append_object_record_byte
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: int append_object_record_byte(unsigned char value, short tag)
note: append_object_record_bytes(&value,1,tag); returns 1 (bytes written)

name: append_object_record_word
note: byte-swaps the low 16 bits of value (FUN_0042efb0) and appends them; returns 2

name: append_object_record_long
note: byte-swaps value to big-endian (FUN_0042ef70) and appends 4 bytes; returns 4

name: append_sized_value_to_data_record
note: size_code 0/1/2 = byte/word/long read from *value, appended to a data record (tag 0x1c); returns 1/2/4 (uninitialised for another code). Callers FUN_00417bfa, FUN_00424a19, FUN_00424cc4, FUN_0042861d (add the result to the section location counter)

name: append_sized_value_to_repeat_data_record
note: as append_sized_value_to_data_record but with the value itself and tag 0x9c; returns 1/2/4. Only caller FUN_00424a19, which writes 0xc0, the location, a repeat count, the unit size and the value as one 0x9c record when the count is >= 2 (hence "repeat")

name: append_object_record_bytes
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void append_object_record_bytes(unsigned char *data, int len, unsigned int tag)
note: the object file record buffer (g_object_record_start/pos/end): a new tag (or g_object_record_force_new) closes the current record with finish_object_record (marking it 0x80 when the low 7 bits of the tag change); a fresh record gets the tag byte & 0x7f and a length slot; a 0x1c record also gets 0x80 and the big-endian location counter of the current section, and is preceded by a section select record (build_section_select_record, closed as 0x1a) when g_object_need_section_select is set; data that does not fit is split over records except for tags 0x1c (<= 4 bytes), 0x30, 0x34, 0x38, 0x3a, 0x40. data NULL/len 0 with tag 0xff just closes. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: finish_object_record
note: if the record buffer is not empty: stores the length byte (size+1) at start[1]; for tag 0x1c adds the size to g_section_data_bytes, stores the data length (size-8) at start[7] and advances the current section's location counter g_section_location_counter[kind] by it; appends compute_object_record_checksum and writes the record to g_object_file (FUN_0042ef00, error 0xce7); resets pos to start. Callers append_object_record_bytes, run_assembler_passes (0x7f at the end). Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: compute_object_record_checksum
note: ~(sum of the record bytes from g_object_record_start to pos, as a short); caller finish_object_record stores its low byte

name: append_reloc_expression_byte
note: SIG kept (takes the address of its own stack argument): append_reloc_expression_bytes(&value,1); returns its result

name: append_reloc_expression_word
note: SIG kept: byte-swaps the low 16 bits in place, append_reloc_expression_bytes(&value,2)

name: append_reloc_expression_long
note: SIG kept: byte-swaps to big-endian in place, append_reloc_expression_bytes(&value,4)

name: append_reloc_entry_header
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: int append_reloc_entry_header(int address, short bit_width, int flag)
note: SIG kept (third stack argument). Writes a flag byte (3 when flag == 0, | (bit_width*2-0x10) when request byte +0x2a is set, | 4), the 4-byte address, then the field layout: request +0x2a clear: 0, bit_width; else 8/16/32-bit layouts as (offset,width) bytes. Only caller FUN_00427769, which follows it with the expression terms (symbol refs via FUN_00427942, 0x20/0x21/0x24/0x25 operators, 0xff end), patches the entry length and commits it (append_reloc_expression_bytes(NULL,0)). The returned value is not used

name: append_reloc_expression_bytes
note: appends len bytes to the relocation expression buffer (g_reloc_expr_pos, error 0x1360 past g_reloc_expr_end); data NULL commits the buffered entry (g_reloc_expr_start..pos) to the relocation record buffer (append_reloc_record_bytes) and resets pos. Ghidra return undefined; kept 4 bytes (ret4: the write pointer) because append_reloc_expression_byte/word/long return it (no caller uses it further)

name: append_reloc_record_bytes
note: appends len bytes to the relocation record buffer (g_reloc_record_pos), flushing it first (flush_reloc_records) when they do not fit before g_reloc_record_end. Caller append_reloc_expression_bytes. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: flush_reloc_records
note: writes the relocation record buffer as object records of tag 0x20 (append_object_record_bytes), resets it and sets g_object_need_section_select (the next data record must re-select its section). Callers run_assembler_passes (end), emit_final_asm_record_stream, FUN_00417bfa, FUN_00424a19, FUN_00424cc4, FUN_00425a51, FUN_00425fbc, FUN_0042861d

name: read_backend_record_payload
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned int read_backend_record_payload(FILE *stream, psd *rec, unsigned char op)
note: saves stream in g_backend_stream and reads the rest of a record whose op byte was read, by the payload format g_backend_op_payload_format[op] (u16 per op): 1/7 none; 2..6, 10..12 fixed byte counts into psd fields (+8..+0x17); 8 = an instruction: 4 bytes to +0xc, 4 to +8, flg (&0xe3), misc (&0xa0), then 0/1/2 operands (read_record_operand(rec,1/2)), error 0x131e otherwise; 9 = pseudo-op (read_pseudo_op_record_payload). Unknown format: error 0x131d. Returns the byte count / nonzero, 0xffffffff on a short read. Callers read_next_backend_record (.sub/.sua records), run_assembler_passes (the leading section record 0xc..0xf)

name: read_backend_stream_bytes
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned int read_backend_stream_bytes(char *buf, unsigned int count)
note: FUN_0042eea0(g_backend_stream, buf, count) (fread wrapper), error 0xce6 on -1; returns the count read. Callers: the backend record readers 00402b00..00404596

name: read_pseudo_op_record_payload
note: payload of the pseudo-ops 0x22..0x31 (OP_RETURN .. OP_EXTST, enums.tsv): 8 header bytes to +0xc (filno/linno) and +8 (expno), then per op: RETURN/CALL/JUMP/JUMPT/JUMPF a label operand (read_branch_label_operand; CALL also a misc byte &0x80, the jumps a tmp byte); MV_LOC/MVA_LC: register + @(disp,FP) (reg 0x6c) operands; MVA_PC/MOVI/MVA_FC/MOVIF: #imm source (kind 7) with label refs (read_operand_label_refs) and a register destination (MOVI's register is the third payload byte, notes "late _init_slow_flag"); FPRSET two registers; EXTLD/EXTST @Rn <-> reg 0x60. Allocates 0xc-byte ea operands (FUN_0040cf00, error 0xbcd); unknown op error 0x131f. Returns 0xffffffff on a short read. Caller read_backend_record_payload (format 9)

name: read_record_operand
note: allocates an ea (0xc) as rec->ea1 (which 1) or rec->ea2 (which 2, else error 0x131e) and reads it: a kind byte (&0x1f, |0x80 flag), then per kind: 1..4, 0xf, 0x10 register byte; 5 control register (byte + 0x61 = REG_SR..); 6 system register (byte + 0x64 = REG_MACH..); 7 #imm of the record's operand size (operand_size_from_flags, store_immediate_in_operand; AND/OR/TST/XOR/TRAPA keep only the low byte) followed by a label-ref count (read_operand_label_refs); 8 @(disp,Rn) register + s16 disp; 9 @(R0,Rn) index<<4|base nibbles; 10 @(disp,PC) s16 disp, base REG_PC; 11 @(disp,GBR) 4-byte disp + label refs, base REG_GBR; 12 @(R0,GBR) index byte, base REG_GBR; other kinds error 0x1320. Caller read_backend_record_payload (format 8)

name: read_branch_label_operand
note: reads a 2-byte label number and makes rec->ea1 an #imm operand (kind 7) whose label_ref list (one 8-byte label_ref, labno1 = the label) names it. Caller read_pseudo_op_record_payload (RETURN, CALL, JUMP, JUMPT, JUMPF)

name: operand_size_from_flags
note: rec->flg & 3: 0/1/2 -> 1/2/4 bytes; error 0x1321 otherwise (result uninitialised). Caller read_record_operand (#imm operands)

name: store_immediate_in_operand
note: stores a 1/2/4-byte immediate (the bytes at value) into op->disp (+4..+7), sign-extending 1 and 2 byte values; error 0x1322 for another size. Callers read_record_operand, read_pseudo_op_record_payload (MV_LOC). Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: read_operand_label_refs
note: reads count 2-byte label numbers (error 0x1323 on a short read) into op->labels: pairs fill labno1 then labno2 of the last label_ref (labno1 - labno2 differences), a new 8-byte label_ref is appended when the last one is full. Callers read_record_operand, read_pseudo_op_record_payload

name: compare_bytes
note: qsort comparator: *a vs *b ascending (0 / -1 / 1). Passed to sort_array by build_sh4_dependency_graph for the per-entry register lists

name: compare_order_entries_by_height
note: qsort comparator on the 0xc-byte entries of g_sh4_order_table: height (+4) descending. Passed to sort_array by FUN_00406ac1 (list scheduler: highest critical-path height first)

name: compare_order_entries_by_index
note: qsort comparator on g_sh4_order_table entries: window index byte (+1) ascending. Passed (PUSH 0x40479a) to sort_array by the debug dump FUN_0040ba89 ("Scheduled Easy View")

name: compare_superscalar_entries_by_issue_order
note: qsort comparator on the 0xe0-byte g_sh4_window entries: issue order byte (+0x18, set by the scheduler FUN_00406ac1) ascending, signed. Passed to sort_array by drain_next_sh4_scheduled_record

name: read_next_superscalar_scheduled_record
note: Existing name read_next_pipeline_buffered_backend_record was misleading: it does not use the pipeline() window; with request->cpu == 4 (SH-4) read_next_backend_record reads through it, it fills the 0xe0-byte superscalar window (g_superscalar_window), schedules it (schedule_superscalar_window) and returns the scheduled records one at a time (s01).

name: drain_next_superscalar_scheduled_record
note: sets g_sh4_draining, sorts g_sh4_window by issue order (sort_array with compare_sh4_entries_by_issue_order; every call), copies entry g_sh4_drain_index's record to rec and advances; when g_sh4_drain_count is reached clears g_sh4_draining and the index. Returns rec. Callers read_next_pipeline_buffered_backend_record, read_next_backend_record (while g_sh4_draining)

name: sort_array
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void sort_array(void *base, int count, int size, void *compare)
note: qsort-style: packs {base, size, compare} in a local sort_context and runs quicksort_range(1, count, &ctx). Callers drain_next_sh4_scheduled_record, build_sh4_dependency_graph, FUN_00406ac1, FUN_0040ba89. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: quicksort_range
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void quicksort_range(int first, int last, sort_context *ctx)
note: recursive quicksort of elements first..last (1-based) of ctx->base (element size ctx->size, comparator ctx->compare(a,b) < 0 = a before b), swapping byte by byte and following the pivot when it moves; recurses into the smaller part. Caller sort_array, itself. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: run_superscalar_scheduler
note: when the window has more than one record: clears every entry's scheduling fields (FUN_0040728c), analyses each entry (FUN_00407518, index in the global g_sh4_analyze_index), builds the dependency graph and heights (build_sh4_dependency_graph), dumps the original order when request byte +0x13c & 8 (FUN_00406664 -> FUN_0040ba89(1)), list-schedules (FUN_00406ac1, sets the +0x18 issue order). Caller read_next_pipeline_buffered_backend_record

name: build_superscalar_dependency_graph
note: for g_sh4_window entries 0..g_pipeline_window_last_index: sorts each read-register (+0x20, count +0x1e) and written-register (+0x38, count +0x1f) list (compare_bytes); forward pass: a register written by i and read by a later j = flow edge (child mask +0xbc / count +0xb8 on i, parent mask +0xc0 / count +0xb9 on j), written again by a later j = output ("ambi") edge (+0xd4/+0xd0, +0xd8/+0xd1) and stop; memory edges via FUN_004059f8; backward pass: written by i and read by an earlier j = anti edge (+0xc8/+0xc4 on j, +0xcc/+0xc5 on i); stores (issue class 0x11..0x15 LSs) against earlier loads (0xc..0x10 LSl, not @(disp,PC)) sharing a register = ambi edges; finally the height (+0x54) of each entry from the end: max(height of flow children + latency (+0x50, 1 when 0), height of anti children + 1). Masks use g_window_entry_bit_masks (0x80000000 >> i). Dumps the table (FUN_0040ba89(0): "Data Dependency List", "FlowChild AntiChild AmbiChild", ...) when request byte +0x13c & 8. Caller schedule_sh4_window. Ghidra return undefined (ret4 value unused)

name: add_store_memory_order_dependencies
note: For every superscalar-window entry whose issue_group (+0x51) is a store class 0x11..0x15, adds an "ambi" (ordering) dependency with every other load/store-class entry (group 7..0x15): the earlier of the pair gets the later's bit in ambi_child_mask (+0xd4) and ambi_child_count++ (+0xd0); the later gets the earlier's bit in ambi_parent_mask (+0xd8) and ambi_parent_count++ (+0xd1). Bits from g_bit_mask_msb_first. Iterates g_pipeline_window_last_index..0. Only caller: FUN_00404fc5 (builds the register flow/anti/ambi dependencies, then calls this). Window = g_superscalar_window (0044bcb0, 32 x 0xe0).

name: rewrite_entry_expression_with_earlier_definitions
note: Sets expr_rewritten (+0x52)=1; if the entry's expr_text (+0x98) is non-empty, points expr (+0xdc) at it, then walks earlier entries entry-1..0: takes their defs_text (+0x58, "lhs=rhs" pairs separated by ':') or, when empty, their expr_text (returns when both are empty), splits each pair at '=' and replaces the first occurrence of lhs in the current expression by rhs (replace_first_substring); each successful replacement becomes the new expr (malloc'd, never freed). NO CALLERS in the export (dead code; the unfinished memory disambiguation, with 00405f44).

name: entries_access_disjoint_memory
note: 0 when either entry's expr_text (+0x98) is empty. Splits each entry's rewritten expression (*(+0xdc)) into terms at '+','-','=' (dropping '@','(',')'; at most 64 terms of 64 bytes: 8 KB of stack, hence _chkstk FUN_00435020). Term counts differ: 0. Access size from rec.flg&3 (2->4, 1->2, else 1 byte). Returns 0xff ("disjoint") only when both offsets are >0 and the byte ranges [off, off+size) do not overlap; otherwise runs a strncmp-like loop over the terms (FUN_00435000, result unused) and returns 0. The offset read is the SIGNED BYTE at +2 of rec.ea1 (ea.index in types.h): see the lead note. NO CALLERS (dead code). Return kept 4 bytes.

name: replace_first_substring
note: strlen (FUN_00434da0) of all three; NULL if find is longer than str, if strstr (FUN_0042efd0) finds no match, or if malloc (FUN_00435050) of len(str)-len(find)+len(repl)+1 fails; otherwise a new string = prefix + repl + rest after the match. Only caller: rewrite_entry_expression_with_earlier_definitions. Ghidra's params were uint* (4 bytes, used as byte strings).

name: compute_original_order_issue_cycles
note: Debug path only: FUN_00404f53 calls it when request +0x13c & 8 (the pipeline-dump flag). Walks the superscalar window in ORIGINAL order with a per-entry latency countdown (char[32], 0 = done): an entry stalls while a flow parent (+0xc0), anti parent (+0xcc) or ambi parent (+0xd8) still counts down; an issued entry gets countdown = latency (+0x50) and its cycle in g_superscalar_order[i].cycle (0044e168 + i*0xc); the next entry issues in the same cycle when it is also ready and issue_groups_conflict() == 0 (dual issue). Ends with FUN_0040ba89(1), which prints "Original Easy View".

name: schedule_superscalar_window
note: The scheduler of this path (FUN_00404f53 always calls it). Fills g_superscalar_order[i] = {issued 0, entry i, path_length (+0x54)}, sorts by path_length descending (FUN_00404ce6, qsort-like, comparator FUN_00404737 on +4), then for up to 200 cycles: decrements latency countdowns; picks the first unissued slot (highest path) whose flow parents are not busy and whose flow/anti/ambi parents are all issued (+0x19); marks it (order +0x18 = running issue number, scheduled +0x19 = 1, slot.issued = 1, slot.cycle = cycle); then tries a second ready entry that issue_groups_conflict() lets pair with it. Stops when every slot is issued. Dumps FUN_0040ba89(2) "Scheduled Easy View" when request +0x13c & 8.

name: issue_groups_conflict
note: 0xff when the issue groups (+0x51) of the two window entries cannot issue in the same cycle, 0 when they can: either is 4; both 1; a==6 and b is 6 or 5; a==5; both in 7..0x15; both 2. Callers compare the whole value with 0 (compute_original_order_issue_cycles, schedule_superscalar_window): keep int. Matches the SH-4 dual-issue rules (groups in types_proposal.h).

name: clear_superscalar_window_analysis
note: For entries 0..g_pipeline_window_last_index clears the fields after the psd record: order (+0x18) = 0xff, scheduled, read/write counts and register lists, latency/group/flag, path_length, defs_text and expr_text (0x40 bytes each from +0x58 and +0x98; the second runs to +0xd8 and is re-cleared by the later stores), the flow/anti/ambi counts and masks. Leaves +0x1a..+0x1d (operand registers/kinds, set when the record is loaded, FUN_0040b3e0) and +0xdc. Only caller: FUN_00404f53 (first step).

name: describe_superscalar_window_entry
note: For window entry g_superscalar_current_entry (FUN_00404f53 loops it over 0..last) switches on rec.op (MOV, FMOV, FADD, FDIV, FSQRT, FLOAT, FLDI0/1, FSTS/FLDS, BF/BT/..., RTE, TRAPA, SLEEP, SETT, NOP, ...) and the operand registers/kinds (+0x1a..+0x1d); records registers read (FUN_0040ad6c: read_regs +0x20, count +0x1e; FPSCR 0x68 for FPU ops, TBIT 0x6d, SSR/SPC for RTE) and written (FUN_0040b055: +0x38/+0x1f); builds the definition texts ("Rn=@(Rm)", "Rn=IMM", "Rm=4+Rm"... from the strings 0043c508..0043c640 and the register-name table 0043ecc8) and stores latency, issue group, a third value (to 0044d8f0[entry]) and both texts with FUN_0040b33e. Branches, RTE, TRAPA etc. make every other entry their flow child (barrier). Only caller: FUN_00404f53.

name: add_superscalar_entry_read_register
note: appends regno to the read-register list (+0x20, count +0x1e) of g_sched_window[g_sched_current_index] (0xe0-byte sched_entry at 0044bcb0); expands groups to single registers: 0x20..0x2e (DRn) -> regno-0x10, regno-0xf; 0x30..0x3c (FVn) -> 4 regs from regno-0x20; 0x50..0x5e (XDn) -> regno-0x40, regno-0x3f; 0x60 (XMTRX) -> 0x10..0x1f; else regno itself. Only caller FUN_00407518 (per-op register/latency analysis; passes 'h' = FPSCR 0x68, 'g' = FPUL 0x67)

name: add_superscalar_entry_written_register
note: twin of add_sched_entry_read_register for the written-register list (+0x38, count +0x1f) of the current g_sched_window entry; same DR/FV/XD/XMTRX expansion. Only caller FUN_00407518

name: set_superscalar_entry_timing
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void set_superscalar_entry_timing(char latency, char issue_group, int stage_pattern, void *effect_text1, void *effect_text2)
note: current g_sched_window entry: +0x50 = latency (dump column 'Latency', %2d), +0x51 = issue group (dump column 'Kind'; names at 0043f298 ----,EX,FE,MT,CO,CB,BR,LS,LS1..LSs8 = SH-4 issue groups), g_sched_entry_stage_pattern[i] = stage_pattern (Easy View 'Pipeline' column; names at 0043f2f0 EAS,E=S,...), memcpy 0x40 bytes of each text buffer into +0x58 / +0x98 (FUN_00407518 builds texts like "R1=@(R2):R2=R2+8" with strcpy/strcat into 0x40-byte locals). Caller FUN_00407518, e.g. (2, 0xc /*LSl*/, 0, ...) for loads, (1, 0x11 /*LSs*/, ...) for stores. NOTE: the +0x98 copy (0x40 bytes) overlaps the dependency masks at +0xbc..+0xd4 (see types_proposal.h)

name: record_superscalar_entry_operands
