name: pool_alloc
note: zeroed small-block allocation: size must be 1..0x400 and a multiple of 4; finds or adds the size class in g_pool_size_classes (0x108-byte pool_size_class blocks from FUN_00435050 = malloc, 32 classes each, chained at +4), allocates with alloc_from_pool_chunks, zero-fills; message 0xbcd (out of memory) on failure. ~95 call sites with sizes 8/0xc/0x10/0x18/0x20/0x30/0x104; freed by pool_free with the same size. Callers use the result as an address (Ghidra: int)

name: pool_try_alloc
note: identical to pool_alloc but returns 0 without reporting 0xbcd. No callers in the export

name: alloc_from_pool_chunks
note: walks one size class's chunk list: bump-allocates (free_ptr += size while <= end) or pops the chunk's free list (free_count--); if none can serve, prepends a new_pool_chunk and bump-allocates from it; 0 when malloc fails. Callers pool_alloc, pool_try_alloc

name: new_pool_chunk
note: FUN_00435050(0x414) (malloc): next = 0, free_ptr = data (+0x14), end = +0x414, free_list = 0, free_count = 0. Only caller alloc_from_pool_chunks

name: pool_free
note: finds size class `size` in g_pool_size_classes and frees ptr with free_to_pool_chunks; message 0x12e8 when there is no class of that size. ~35 callers (store_request_record_updates frees each section's +0x18 record with size 0x30)

name: free_to_pool_chunks
note: finds the chunk whose data area [end-0x400, end) holds ptr (message 0x12ea if none), message 0x12eb if ptr is already on that chunk's free list (double free), pushes ptr, free_count++; when free_count == 0x400/size unlinks the chunk and releases it with FUN_00435290 (free). Only caller pool_free

name: assemble_instruction
note: one backend record -> instruction word + text: format = g_opcode_format_index[op] or, when 0xff, the alternative-list row matching size (flg&3), ea1/ea2 kind and (ops 0x8c/0x8d/0x9c/0x9d) the register (message 0x1338 when none); prints the mnemonic (format +0x10) on channel 3 (listing, request+6 bit 2) or 2 (.src, request+0x12 != 1); calls the format's two operand encoders (+4/+8) with the field shifts (+0xc..+0xf), flg&3, filno, linno and ORs their bits into the base word (+0); prints "; Line n" when request+0x13c bit 2 (listing, request+4 != 0); for op 0x40 with an @(disp,PC) source calls print_pc_relative_literal_comment; in object mode (request+0x12 == 1) writes the word with FUN_004021b1(word, 0x1c), byte-swapped when request+0x2a == 0; g_location_counter += 2. Callers emit_final_asm_record_stream, FUN_00416ff0. Before that, FUN_0042e064 is applied to both operands (not identified)

name: print_pc_relative_literal_comment
note: for MOV.W/MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn: picks the literal_entry at index (disp - (label record +0x24 - +8 via FUN_00427a7d(labno2 of ea1 labels)))/4 in g_long_literal_pool (size 2) or disp/2 in g_word_literal_pool and prints "; " + "H'" value (FUN_0042375c long / FUN_00423722 word), or for a literal with labels "H'"value (if non-zero) and each label_ref labno1 [+labno2] joined by '+' (FUN_004232ef). Only caller assemble_instruction

name: emit_register_operand
note: operand encoder of g_instruction_format_table for registers (Rn/Rm, control/system registers, FRn; FIPR/FTRV vector registers 0x30/0x34/0x38/0x3c -> 0..3): returns (reg & 0xf) << field_shift (0 when field_shift == -1) and prints the register name (FUN_004234f6) on channel 3/2. Called only through the table (+4/+8); the table passes 6 arguments, Ghidra's 2 kept

name: emit_memory_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_memory_operand(ea *op, int reg_shift, int disp_shift, int size_code, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder for @Rn (kind 2), @(disp,Rn)/@(disp,GBR), @(R0,Rn)/@(R0,GBR) (disp_shift == -1: prints the index register) and @(disp,PC) (kind 10): register bits at reg_shift; displacement = FUN_0042df80 value (PC-relative: minus (g_location_counter+4) & ~3 for size_code 2, & ~1 otherwise) must be a multiple of 1<<size_code (msg 0xc1c) and fit 4 bits (kind 2) / 8 bits after scaling (msg 0x133a; an unresolved external symbol gets a relocation via FUN_00427769 and msg 0xa98, severity 3); prints "@(disp,Rn)" etc. Used by MOV.B/W/L, MOVA, TAS.B, JMP/JSR, PREF, FMOV.S, AND.B/OR.B/TST.B/XOR.B

name: emit_postincrement_operand
note: operand encoder for @Rn+: returns reg << field_shift (callers use the low 16 bits; Ghidra's 4-byte return kept), prints "@", the register, "+". Used by MOV.x @Rm+,Rn, LDS.L/LDC.L, MAC.W/MAC.L, FMOV.S LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_predecrement_operand
note: operand encoder for @-Rn: returns reg << field_shift, prints "@-" (0043c7c4) and the register. Used by MOV.x Rm,@-Rn, STS.L/STC.L, FMOV.S LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_branch_disp8_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_branch_disp8_operand(ea *op, int field_shift, int unused_3, int unused_4, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder for BT/BF/BT/S/BF/S: disp = target (FUN_0042df80) - (g_location_counter + 4); odd -> msg 0x1339, outside -0x100..0xfe -> msg 0x133a; returns ((disp >> 1) & 0xff) << field_shift; prints the target expression (labels via FUN_004272c3 / FUN_00427c99, then FUN_00423453) LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_branch_disp12_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_branch_disp12_operand(ea *op, int field_shift, int unused_3, int unused_4, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder for BRA/BSR: as emit_branch_disp8_operand with range -0x1000..0xffe and a 12-bit field ((disp >> 1) & 0xfff) LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_unsigned_imm8_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_unsigned_imm8_operand(ea *op, int field_shift, int unused_3, int unused_4, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder for #imm of AND/OR/TST/XOR (register and .B @(R0,GBR) forms): value (FUN_0042df80) must fit 0..0xff (msg 0x133a); returns (value & 0xff) << field_shift; prints '#' and the expression LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_signed_imm8_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_signed_imm8_operand(ea *op, int field_shift, int unused_3, int unused_4, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder for #imm of MOV/ADD/CMP/EQ: value must be -0x80..0x7f (msg 0x133a); an unresolved external symbol (label_ref with labno2 == -0x8000 and no next) gets an 8-bit relocation via FUN_00427769(..., 8, 0, 1), msg 0xa98 (severity 3) when out of range; returns (value & 0xff) << field_shift; prints '#' and the expression LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: emit_trapa_imm8_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: unsigned short emit_trapa_imm8_operand(ea *op, int field_shift, int unused_3, int unused_4, short filno, unsigned int linno)
note: operand encoder used only by TRAPA (format c300): the constant ea.disp (no labels) must fit 0..0xff (msg 0x133a); returns (disp & 0xff) << field_shift; prints '#' and the number LOW HALF: returns 2 bytes; the stock code leaves a leftover in the high half (CONCAT22) and its only caller, assemble_instruction (through the format table), ORs the result into the 16-bit opcode_word.

name: shcasm_main
note: (already named) argv[1] is the request record path (load_request_record_file(4, argv[1]), store_request_record_updates(argv[1])); argc unused. Also sets g_current_request_copy and runs FUN_00429060 (first layout pass) between load_intermediate_record_stream and run_assembler_passes; exits via FUN_004352e0(severity * 2 + 1)

name: store_request_record_updates
note: (already named) request+0xac = DAT_0044a6dc; pool_free(section +0x18, 0x30) for each section of the request+0x24 list (next at +0x1c); request+0xe4/+0xe8 = DAT_0044bc5c/DAT_0044a8ea; store_request_record_file(4, path), msg 0x1325 on failure

name: emit_debug_information
note: Existing name emit_final_object_file was wrong: run_assembler_passes calls it only for object output (request +0x12 == 1) with debug information (request +0x16). Closes the debug scopes, opens the .db1 (request +0x78) and .db2 (request +0x7c) temp files "rb", rewinds the line-range/stack-offset/register-map temp files, writes the object header (emit_object_header_and_tables) and translates the .db1 records (tags 0x32..0x50) into object debug records (s04).

name: emit_object_header_and_tables
note: name kept (already given). Called by emit_final_object_file before its record loop. Appends (FUN_00402374 = append bytes to the stream-1 object record of a tag) tag 0x30: 'H' ('h' when request+4), word g_object_header_word, word g_section_count; one 10-byte tag-0x30 section entry per used section (section number from the section_group +0x18 table, u32 0, u32 size section_group->size[kind]; only group 0 kind 0 when g_program_has_content is 0) plus the extra section when g_extra_section_needed; the language tag as a counted string (C_SH / C++ tag by request+0x144); 12 date bytes YYMMDDhhmmss from the request's date text (+0xf0.., month via month_name_to_digits). Then tag 0x40: word 0x1001 (g_debug_word_1001), count of the request+0xec source-file list, per file id 1..count a 0 byte and the counted full path (FUN_0042ef50, else the stored name of length entry+6; message 0x1358 when an id is missing), word 0 terminator.

name: translate_scope_record
note: emit_final_object_file case 0x32 (body at g_temp_record_cursor). Byte 0: scope kind (low 7 bits; 0 compilation unit, 3 function, 4 and 9 inner blocks) with 0x80 = scope end. Begin: g_debug_scope_depth++, pushes the next child scope_node on g_scope_stack (g_scope_top++), writes tag 0x32: kind, request+4 byte, section number (symbol+0x1a of the function symbol g_debug_function_symbol via FUN_00427a7d; 0 for kind 0), u32 start, u32 size (end - start; for kind 0 the sum of the section_group sizes), a byte, a frame byte (0x80 + u32 return-address offset -(FUN_0042ec79 saved words*4+4) for a non-leaf, non-interrupt function; 0x40 interrupt; 0x60 + 4 bytes read from g_stack_offset_file for an interrupt with a stack switch, consuming one aux_record+0x1c count), then a word. Kind 3 then: emit_stack_offset_records, a kind-4 inner scope begin when request+4, FUN_00401000 (load the function's debug symbol and location tables) once per function (g_function_debug_loaded). A kind-3 begin while g_drop_function_debug is set instead skips temp records up to the next kind-3 scope record and frees the debug symbols (FUN_0040156c). End: g_debug_scope_depth--; kind 3 with request+4: emit_block_scope_records then an 0x84 end; pops the scope stack; writes the 1-byte end record; kind 3 frees the tables (FUN_0040156c, FUN_00401655) and clears g_function_debug_loaded.

name: emit_block_scope_records
note: Called by translate_scope_record at a function's end (request+4 path). While the current scope_node has a child: push it, write a tag-0x32 block begin (kind 9, request+4 byte, function section number, u32 start, u32 size, 1, word 0x1001), then read (symbol id, location id) short pairs from g_block_symbol_file until id -1; for ids <= request+0xb4 or > request+0xb0 look up the debug_symbol (g_debug_symbol_hash, id % 0x7f) and debug_location (g_debug_location_hash) and write a tag-0x34 symbol record: kind byte + id, counted name, word +0xc, then if kind & 1 the location kind, u32 +0x10 and the location (u32 stack offset for kind 6, else counted register name "R%d" / "FR%d"), words +8, +0xa, 0x1001, and for kind 0xe two type bytes; then pop and write 0x89 (block end).

name: emit_stack_offset_records
note: Called by translate_scope_record at a function scope begin. Writes tag 0x3a: word (g_debug_function_symbol - 0xb6), u32 count = aux_record+0x1c of the function (FUN_00427a7d(g_debug_function_symbol)->aux_index into g_aux_record_table), then copies count 8-byte entries from g_stack_offset_file (FUN_0041e4b5 writes (address, stack offset) pairs there when the offset changes and increments aux+0x1c). Message 0xce6 on a read error.

name: translate_debug_symbol_record
note: emit_final_object_file case 0x34. Byte 0 = kind<<1 | has_location, word symbol id (+0xb6 = symbol number; kind 3 sets g_debug_function_symbol), name length (the name itself is read from g_object_record_input). Location kinds 2/3/4 refer to an asm symbol (hash 0044ab30, number % 0x3fd): missing -> g_suppress_debug_record and g_drop_function_debug set; 2/4 write the symbol's section number (+0x1a) and value (+8); 2/3 add a separate record with the name prefixed '_'. Kind 0xe, or kind 0 with location 1/6: finds or creates the debug_symbol (FUN_0040cf00(0x20), g_debug_symbol_hash) and writes its location (6 = u32 stack offset, 1 = counted register name R%d / FR%d / DR%d). Then kind 7: byte + 2 or 3 u32; kind 8: counted bytes; word value-1 (also stored at debug_symbol+8), two words; kind 9: a byte; kind 0xe: type bytes from debug_symbol+0x1c (u32 or register name). Nothing is written while g_suppress_debug_record is set (cleared on entry when g_debug_group_depth is 0).

name: translate_tag4e_record
note: emit_final_object_file case 0x4e. Copies with byte swapping (FUN_0042ef70 u32, FUN_0042efb0 u16; host order -> big endian): u32, count byte, count x (byte, byte, u32, byte, u32), word; writes it under the input tag unless g_suppress_debug_record. What the record describes is not established.

name: translate_tag44_record
note: emit_final_object_file case 0x44. Copies kind byte, u32 (swapped), byte, an extra word when kind is 10 or 11, then a word; writes under the input tag unless g_suppress_debug_record. What the record describes is not established.

name: translate_short_tagged_record
note: emit_final_object_file cases 0x36, 0x48, 0x4a, 0x4c, 0x50 (tag = the input record's tag byte). Except for 0x50 copies a leading byte and stops after it when the record's first byte has bit 0x80 (end form); 0x48 copies a second byte; then one word (swapped). Writes under the tag unless g_suppress_debug_record. Tag 0x36 nests: first byte 0 = begin (g_debug_group_depth++), else end (g_debug_group_depth--, at 0 clears g_suppress_debug_record).

name: emit_spooled_tag38_records
note: Called by emit_final_object_file after its record loop. Tag 0x38: word count (DAT_0044d8e4, entries spooled by FUN_0041fcb9), then per entry the 16-byte header read back from the temp file DAT_0044d8bc (opened by FUN_0041e360) and as many 4-byte items as the header's word at +0xe; then the word 0x1001. What the entries describe is not established (FUN_0041fcb9 builds them from the 0x18-byte list at DAT_0044bc64).

name: run_assembler_passes
note: name kept (already given).

name: emit_object_module_header_record
note: run_assembler_passes, object output only (request+0x12 == 1). Builds the tag-4 record in g_module_header_record (0x1c bytes): 0x20 (0x28 when request+0x2a), date YYMMDDhhmmss from the request date text, word 1, 0, "0200", 8, 0x20, 0x20, five zero bytes; then the counted module name (get_module_name) and the counted CPU name "SH" (pointer at 00443040), all under tag 4.

name: emit_object_unit_record
note: run_assembler_passes, object output only. Tag 6 from g_unit_record: 0x40, words g_section_count, DAT_0044bc5c, DAT_0044a8ea (the counts store_request_record_updates writes to request+0xe4 / +0xe8); the counted module name; the counted language tag (C / C++ by request+0x144); the 12 date bytes at g_module_header_record+1.

name: emit_section_definition_record
note: run_assembler_passes calls it per used (group, kind) in section-number order (kind 0..3 = the four section kinds whose default names are request+0x50..+0x5c). Object output only: flushes, then tag 8 from g_section_record: 0x40, u32 0, u32 size group->size[kind] (Ghidra: short* param_2 + kind*2 + 4 = byte +8 + kind*4), u32 alignment (0x20 for kind 0 with request+0x13d & 8; 0x10 for kind 0 with request+0x14b; 8 for kind != 0 when request+0x18 == 4; else 4), attribute byte (0 kind 0 / 0x10 kinds 1..3), word 0xffc0; then the section name (FUN_00427d94) as length byte (FUN_00402180) + text.

name: emit_object_record_kind_table
note: run_assembler_passes, object output only. Writes the 0x1e-byte table at 00440d00 (request+0x16 set) or 00440d20 (not set) under tag 0: one byte per index, 0x80 or 0; the request+0x16 variant also marks indexes 0x0c..0x1a. Read as the record kinds present in the object, the debug kinds only with debug information (request+0x16 also gates emit_final_object_file); the code itself only copies the table.

name: copy_to_counted_string
note: Copies the NUL-terminated text to out+1 and stores its length (one byte) in out[0]. Callers: emit_object_header_and_tables, emit_object_module_header_record, emit_object_unit_record (language tag, CPU name).

name: month_name_to_digits
note: Writes the two ASCII digits of a 3-letter month name: Jan 01, Feb 02, Mar 03, Apr 04, May 05, Jun 06, Jul 07, Aug 08, Sep 09, Oct 10, Nov 11, anything else 12. Called with request+0xf3 (the month of the request's date text "dd Mmm yyyy hh:mm:ss" at +0xf0) by emit_object_header_and_tables and emit_object_module_header_record.

name: get_module_name
note: Counted string (length byte + text) of the output file name request+0x3c without its directory (FUN_00434460; message 0x132e when it fails) and up to the first '.'. Callers: emit_object_module_header_record, emit_object_unit_record.

name: open_output_stream
note: run_assembler_passes: 3 when request+6 & 2 (listing), then 1 (request+0x12 == 1, object) or 2 (== 2, assembler source). Allocates the g_streams[stream] buffer (size at +0x10; stream 3's size = request+8 line width, 0x84 when 0, + 2; message 0xbcd); fopen(get_output_stream_path(stream), mode at +0x18: 1 "wb", 2 "w", 3 "a"; message 0xce4); state 1; cursor = end for an 'r' mode, else base. Stream 1: end -= 1 and two more (size-3)-byte buffers (g_object_data_buffer, g_object_stage_buffer, each with cursor and end). Stream 2: end -= 2, line filled with spaces, g_text_columns = line+0, +10, +0x16, +0x21. Stream 3: end -= 2, spaces, listing fields g_listing_section_field (+0), g_listing_location_field (+4), g_listing_code_field (+0xd), g_listing_mark_field (+0x18), g_text_columns = +0x1a, +0x24, +0x30, +0x3b; resets the code-overflow lines (DAT_0044bc54 = -1, DAT_00448230 = 0, DAT_0044bb28 = 10), g_listing_page = 0, g_listing_page_lines = request+0xc - 4.

name: get_output_stream_path
note: open_output_stream: request+0x3c for streams 1 and 2 (the output file), request+0x38 for 3 (the listing); other values return an uninitialised local (never passed).

name: close_output_stream
note: run_assembler_passes at the end (3 when listing, then 1 or 2): frees the g_streams[stream] buffer (for stream 1 also g_object_data_buffer and g_object_stage_buffer) and fcloses it (message 0xce5).

name: allocate_spool_buffer
note: Called by FUN_0042926d. Allocates g_streams[0] (the "wb+" temp spool, 0x1000 bytes): cursor = base, end = base + size; message 0xbcd. Its FILE is created lazily by FUN_004138e9 (write a byte, FUN_0042f040) and FUN_0041399e flushes and rewinds it.

name: read_spool_byte
note: Returns the next byte of the g_streams[0] spool, sign-extended, refilling the buffer with fread when the cursor reaches the end (message 0xce6). Callers: the per-op expanders FUN_00416ff0, 00419b8d (s06: expand_call), 0041a148, 0041a67b, 0041a982, 0041c4d9, 0041ca2c, 0041cd09, 0041d1e0, 0041d57a; s06 reads it as the branch-form byte stream.

name: record_size_decision_byte
note: appends one byte to g_buffered_streams[0] (the sizing-pass decision stream); when the 0x1000-byte buffer is full it creates the temp file on first use (FUN_0042f040 tmp file, msg 0xce4), writes the buffer out (FUN_0042ef00, msg 0xce7) and restarts at the buffer start. Callers (00420a51, 004218bd, 00421d5b, 00421ffd, 004227c2, 00422b68, 004281b0) call it only when their pass argument is 1 and write the branch/switch form they chose (0 short, 1/2/3 long forms; switch: 1 = 2-byte table) and the two bytes (FUN_0042efb0 byte swap) of a label number they just created with create_symbol_entry; the final pass reads them back with FUN_004137e8

name: rewind_size_decision_stream
note: switches g_buffered_streams[0] from writing to reading: if it spilled to the temp file, writes out the bytes still buffered (msg 0xce7), sets cur = end (so the first FUN_004137e8 read refills) and seeks the file to 0 (FUN_00435430(f,0,0), msg 0x1356); otherwise resets cur to the buffer start. Only caller 00429605 (end of the sizing pass, closes other files)

name: free_size_decision_stream_buffer
note: clears g_buffered_streams[0].spilled and frees its buffer (FUN_00435290); called once from run_assembler_passes after the final pass. The temp file itself is not closed here

name: load_intermediate_record_stream
note: name kept (correct). Opens path (FUN_00435500, g_intermediate_file), allocates the symbol table (request +0xac entries x 0x2c, g_symbol_table) and the section table (request +0x110 entries x 0x44, g_section_table), clears the 0x3fd-bucket hash g_symbol_hash; reads records by a 1-byte header (low 5 bits kind, bits 0xc0 flags): kinds 1..5,7..0xb are symbols (8 bytes: id, aux word, position; a length-prefixed name for kind > 4; attribute byte + extra byte for kind > 6), 0xc a section (many fields, a list of 0x10-byte nodes, name; copies name/section index/attributes to the symbol of the same id), 0xd end (reads g_next_label_number), 0xe three header fields; msg 0x131a/0x131b/0x131c on bad input. request is the loaded request record; kept int since no struct exists for it

name: read_intermediate_bytes
note: FUN_0042eea0(g_intermediate_file, buf, size) (fread-like), msg 0xce6 on -1; callers load_intermediate_record_stream and read_intermediate_string

name: read_intermediate_string
note: reads a 1-byte length then that many bytes into a 0x100-byte string pool chunk (g_string_pool_chunk/_cursor/_end; a new chunk from FUN_00435050(0x100) when it does not fit, msg 0xbcd), NUL-terminates; returns the string, 0 for length 0 (names are length-prefixed in .asb; notes/shcasm.md)

name: find_symbol_entry_by_id
note: walks g_symbol_hash[id % 0x3fd] following +0x14 until +6 == id; returns 0 if absent. Caller load_intermediate_record_stream (kind 0xc: msg 0x131b when missing). Return type: int if symbol_entry (types_proposal.h) is not adopted

name: read_next_scheduled_pipeline_record
note: name kept (correct). Returns 0 with g_pipeline_end_of_stream set when the window is empty (last index -1) or the end was reached; else runs pipeline() first if g_pipeline_reload_pending, copies the head entry's record (g_pipeline_first_scheduled) to rec, release_pipeline_entry_successors, advances along pipeline_entry.next (-2: list now empty), clear_pipeline_entry_and_dependencies, schedule_pipeline_window, run_pipeline_until_stable, counts g_pipeline_drained_count; returns rec. Caller read_next_backend_record uses the result as a pointer

name: pipeline
note: name kept (the stage's own name: "pipetbl dump after pipeline()"). load_pipeline_window; on 0, or when the input ended (no lookahead record and no C_JMP), sets g_pipeline_input_exhausted; when the last window entry is a branch/RTS/RTE/TRAPA (0x8e,0x90..0x9a,0x9e), the window ended with C_JMP (g_pipeline_window_ended_at_c_jmp, cleared here) or the lookahead record is a label (0x18..0x1b), sets g_pipeline_window_ends_block; then mark_pipeline_tail_barrier, build_pipeline_dependency_graph, schedule_pipeline_window, run_pipeline_until_stable, optional dump (request +0x13c & 8)

name: load_pipeline_window
note: name kept (correct). Returns the last entry it filled (pipeline() reads its op byte), 0 when none (Ghidra: undefined *, pointer width kept). reset_pipeline_state; takes g_pipeline_lookahead_record or reads one (read_next_backend_record(..,1)); leading labels (0x18..0x1b), then records up to a branch/label/C_JMP/B_ASM (max 32); a branch joins the window and the next record becomes the lookahead; a C_JMP joins and sets g_pipeline_window_ended_at_c_jmp; other stoppers become the lookahead; sets g_pipeline_window_last_index, compute_pipeline_operand_masks, compute_pipeline_opcode_masks_and_flags

name: compute_pipeline_opcode_masks_and_flags
note: name kept, but it computes the DESTINATION side: the operand named by g_pipeline_op_written_operand (1 ea1, 2 ea2) goes to setreg when a register operand, else to refreg with flags 0x4000 (memory written; @-Rn/@Rn+ also set the base register); op-implied: MUL/MULS/MULU/MAC/CLRMAC set word-1 bits 0x0043ce0c|0x0043ce10 (MACH/MACL in the pre-SH-4 numbering 0x44/0x45); SLEEP/TAS/PREF/B_ASM/C_JMP, psd.flg & 0x80, and LDC to SR/VBR set every bit and 0x4000; g_pipeline_op_t_bit_use bit 0 sets T (word-1 bit 31), bit 1 reads it; g_pipeline_op_fpu_flags bit 0 sets word-1 bit 6; writing R15 sets 0x4000. Clearer: compute_pipeline_destination_masks (optional rename)

name: compute_pipeline_operand_masks
note: name kept, but it computes the SOURCE side: operands named by g_pipeline_op_read_operands (1: ea1; 2: ea2 and ea1) go to refreg; a memory source (not kinds 1,5,6,0xf,0x10,7, not MOVA 0x44, not PC-relative kind 10) sets flags 0x8000; @-Rn/@Rn+ also go to setreg; FMAC (0xcc) also reads FR0 (0x0043ce40 = bit of register 0x10). Clearer: compute_pipeline_source_masks (optional rename)

name: accumulate_operand_register_mask
note: name kept. ORs the base register (and the index register of kinds 9 @(R0,Rn) and 0xc @(R0,GBR)) of a non-immediate operand into mask[0] (registers < 0x20, g_register_bit_masks) or mask[1] (registers >= 0x20 via 0x0043ccfc + reg*4: laid out for the pre-SH-4 numbering, so 0x61..0x73 read unrelated globals; the known MACL bug, notes/shcasm.md). param_2 was byte *: callers pass &rec.ea1->type, i.e. the ea itself

name: reset_pipeline_state
note: name kept (correct). Clears first/last scheduled (-1), end/reload/exhausted/ends-block flags, g_pipeline_window_last_index = -1, g_pipeline_hold, edge count, drained count, g_pipeline_load_result_regs, and every window entry (op 0, masks, flags, depend/next -1, count 0)

name: mark_pipeline_tail_barrier
note: name kept (correct). When the window has more than one entry and its last entry is a branch/JSR/RTS/RTE/TRAPA/B_ASM, sets its setreg to all ones and flags |= 0x4000 so every other entry is ordered before it

name: build_pipeline_dependency_graph
note: name kept (correct). For each entry from the last back, for each of the 0x2a mask bits it sets or reads: an edge from the nearest earlier entry that sets that bit; for each bit it sets: edges from every earlier entry that reads it; memory-read (0x8000) or barrier (0x4000) entries follow the nearest earlier barrier; barrier entries follow every earlier memory-read entry. Reads setreg/refreg through raw addresses 0x448ca8/0x448cb0 (g_pipeline_window[i].setreg/refreg)

name: add_pipeline_dependency_edge
note: name kept (correct). Appends an edge (entry = to) to from's depend list unless present, from < 0 or g_pipeline_edge_count reached 0x3e0; increments g_pipeline_window[to].count

name: schedule_pipeline_window
note: name kept (correct). Repeats passes over the ready entries (count 0, next -1, op != 0) committing each that can_schedule_pipeline_entry_now accepts, until a pass refuses as many as the pass before; if nothing has been scheduled, commits the first ready entry regardless

name: pipeline_entry_uses_memory_stage
note: 1 when the entry is MUL/MULS/MULU or either operand is a memory operand (not kinds 1,5,6,0xf,0x10,7), else 0. Only caller can_schedule_pipeline_entry_now, which pairs it with g_pipeline_code_offset mod 4 (instruction fetch vs memory access slot). Ghidra undefined4; the caller compares the whole value with 0

name: can_schedule_pipeline_entry_now
note: name kept (correct). 0 when: it uses a register the previous memory record loads (g_pipeline_load_result_regs; FPU ops with a register destination exempt); MAC is busy (g_pipeline_mac_busy) and it is MUL/MULS/MULU/MAC or LDS/STS MACH/MACL; an FDIV/FSQRT is busy and it is an FPU op (0xb0..0xdf); or (not a label/C_JMP/B_ASM) its memory-stage use does not suit the slot: memory use at offset mod 4 != 0, none at offset mod 4 == 0. Else 1. Ghidra undefined4; the caller compares with 0

name: release_pipeline_entry_successors
note: for every edge on the entry's depend list decrements the successor's count; msg 0x1342 (successor's filno/linno) when it goes negative. Only caller read_next_scheduled_pipeline_record, on the entry being drained (notes/shcasm.md: "unnamed 0x416574 dependency-count walk")

name: clear_pipeline_entry_and_dependencies
note: name kept (correct). Unlinks the entry's edges (entry/next -1) and resets the entry as reset_pipeline_state does

name: commit_scheduled_pipeline_entry
note: name kept (correct). Links the entry after g_pipeline_last_scheduled (next -2 = last); labels (0x18..0x1b): reset the hazard state and seed g_pipeline_code_offset from the low byte of the label symbol's position (FUN_00427a7d(...)+8); branches/JSR/RTS/RTE/TRAPA +4 (with delay slot), B_ASM pads to 0 mod 4, C_JMP nothing, others +2; MUL..MAC set g_pipeline_mac_busy = 2, LDS/STS MACH/MACL clear it, others count it down; FDIV/FSQRT set their busy counter to 4, non-FPU ops count both down, other FPU ops clear them; g_pipeline_load_result_regs = its setreg when it accesses memory through ea1 or is an FPU op, else 0

name: refill_pipeline_when_drained
note: Existing name run_pipeline_until_stable: it does not loop. When the window is drained (no scheduled entries, g_pipeline_hold 0): sets g_pipeline_reload_pending when the window ended a block, g_pipeline_drained when the stream ended, else loads and schedules the next window (pipeline()).

name: dump_pipeline_table
note: name kept (correct): prints "tbl[%d]:%s :refreg=..." / "flags=%04x, count=%d, next=%d" / "depend =" for every window entry

name: create_symbol_entry
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: symbol *create_symbol_entry(unsigned char kind, unsigned char flags, short id)
note: allocates a 0x2c-byte symbol entry from chunks of 0x588 bytes (8-byte header + 32 entries; g_created_symbol_chunks; FUN_00435050, msg 0xbcd), zeroed; sets kind (+0), flags (+1), id (+6); appends it to its g_symbol_hash chain (+0x14); counts it (chunk +0 entries in chunk, first chunk +2 total). Callers: sizing-pass label creation (kind 2, id = ++g_next_label_number, then record_size_decision_byte of the id) 00420a51 004218bd 00421d5b 00421ffd 00422b68; kind 0xf 004281b0; kind 0xb flags 0x80 00401a14; they fill +8,+0xa,+0xc,+0x10,+0x18 through the result. Ghidra returned short *; keep short * if symbol_entry is not adopted

name: expand_switch_jump
note: emit_final_asm_record_stream's OP_C_JMP case: expands a switch record into code: index -= low bound (int at +0x10; ADD #-low, or MOVI+SUB outside -0x7f..0x80), MOVI #range (int at +0x14) / CMP/HS / JUMPT to the default label (short at +0x0e), SHLL (2-byte table) or SHLL2 (4-byte) chosen by the size byte read back with FUN_004137e8, table address by MOVI label (non-PIC) or MOV + MOVA (request +0x18 != 0), MOV @(R0,Rn), ADD, JMP or BRAF, NOP after BRA/JMP/BRAF/BT_S/BF_S; records built in g_switch_code_records (FUN_0041e2b5/FUN_0041e30b), printed (FUN_0040d7d0; labels FUN_004262e0); then emit_switch_table. The C_JMP record holds ints in the ea1/ea2 slots (+0x10/+0x14) and a label number in the linno slot (+0x0e)

name: emit_switch_table
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void emit_switch_table(short table_label, short base_label, int short_entries)
note: pads by 2 bytes (.RES, offset 0x00447cf0 mod 4) when entries are long or position-independent, emits the table label (FUN_004232ef), reads the table header from g_backend_record_file (1 byte, 2-byte entry count, 2 bytes) and calls emit_switch_table_entry per entry. short_entries = the sizing-pass size byte (1: .DATA.W, 0: .DATA.L)

name: emit_switch_table_entry
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void emit_switch_table_entry(short table_label, short base_label, int short_entries)
note: reads one entry (1 byte, 2-byte case label) from g_backend_record_file and emits it: object output (request +0x12 == 1): the label address (FUN_00427769 relocation) for a long non-PIC table, else label position minus table_label (minus base_label when PIC) through FUN_00402227; listing: ".DATA.L/.W label[-table_label|-base_label]"; advances the section location counter (0x0043cef8[section]) by 2 or 4

name: expand_enter_prologue
note: read_next_backend_record's OP_ENTER case. Looks up the current function (symbol of g_current_function_label, its aux_index +0x10) in g_aux_record_table (0x44-byte aux_record) and appends the prologue to g_expanded_records (g_expanded_record_count++), each record filled by FUN_0041e2b5 (psd: op, flg 2, expno/filno/linno of rec) with operands from FUN_0041e30b (new ea). Interrupt function with a stack switch (flags 0x4000 and a 0x1800 kind): mov.l r0,@-r15; the new stack value by kind (0x1000: mov.l @(sym,GBR),r0 or mov #sym + mov.l @r0,r0; 0x1800: stc gbr,r0 + add #sym; else MOVI via FUN_0041cd09 of stack_value); mov.l r15,@-r0; mov r0,r15. Then mov.l Rn,@-r15 per saved_regs bit (R15 down to R0; R14..R1 when switched), fmov FRn,@-r15 per saved_regs2 (op 0xb0, reg 0x10+n), sts.l PR (unless flags 0x8000), MACH (+0x17 bit 1), MACL (+0x17 bit 0), FPUL (+0x08 bit 0), FPSCR (+0x08 bit 1) (op 0x9d STS); then add #-frame_size,r15 (op 0x60) if frame_size <= 0x80, else MOVI #-frame_size,r0 + add r0,r15 and, when request+0x16 is set, a stack_adjust_node(-frame_size) appended to g_stack_adjust_list.

name: expand_exit_epilogue
note: OP_EXIT case (also called by expand_return). Mirror of expand_enter_prologue: add #(frame_size + sp_adjust),r15 (aux +0x00 plus +0x24; MOVI to r1 + add r1,r15 when >= 0x80, recorded in g_stack_adjust_list under request+0x16); lds.l @r15+ (op 0x8d) for FPSCR, FPUL, MACL, MACH, PR; fmov @r15+ per saved_regs2 from FR0 up; mov.l @r15+,Rn per saved_regs from R0 up (R1..R14 when the stack was switched, then r15 and r0 popped); then RTS (0x96), RTE (0x8e) for an interrupt function (flags 0x4000), or TRAPA #aux+0x16 (0x9e) for flags 0x4000|0x2000. Marks the record before the return with flg 0x40 (delay-slot candidate; read_next_backend_record holds such records back until after the next branch) when request+4 is set, the function is not an interrupt one, and something was restored. Unless rec->flg & 0x10, reads one .lit byte from g_lit_input and sets flg 0x10 (literal pool follows) on the last record when it is 1.

name: expand_return
note: OP_RETURN case. FUN_0042ec79 (saved register word count of the function) < 2: builds a local EXIT record (op 0x21, flg 2|0x10) and calls expand_exit_epilogue (inline epilogue); otherwise builds a JUMP record (op 0x24, tmp register 1, ea1 taken over from rec->ea1, which is cleared) and calls expand_jump (jump to the shared epilogue). Then the same .lit byte -> flg 0x10 step on the last expanded record; the inner calls get flg 0x10 so they do not read it themselves.

name: expand_call
note: OP_CALL case. Call form from the branch-form byte stream (FUN_004137e8): 0 = bsr label (0x93, ea1 = rec->ea1 taken over); 1 = mov.w (flg 1, when FUN_0042ded3 says the target fits the word table) or mov.l @(disp,PC),Rtmp of the target address + jsr @Rtmp (0x95); 2 = mov.l @(disp,PC),Rtmp of a PC-relative distance to a new label (read as 2 bytes, byte-swapped by FUN_0042efb0) + a LABEL record + bsrf Rtmp (0x99). Literals go into g_word_literal_table / g_long_literal_table (FUN_0042d8fa find, FUN_0042dc08 add, FUN_004282e6 index); the operand is @(disp,PC) (ea type 10, base 0x6b) referring to g_literal_pool_label, read from the stream when both tables are empty. Rtmp = rec->tmp. When request+0x16 is set and the target is a runtime routine id <= 0xb6 with a nonzero g_runtime_routine_stack_adjust entry, appends it to g_stack_adjust_list and gives the jsr/bsrf flg 6.

name: expand_jump
note: OP_JUMP case (also called by expand_return and expand_conditional_jump). Same three forms as expand_call: 0 = bra label (0x92); 1 = literal load + jmp @Rtmp (0x94); 2 = PC-relative literal + LABEL + braf Rtmp (0x9a). Then the .lit byte -> flg 0x10 step unless rec->flg & 0x10.

name: expand_conditional_jump
note: OP_JUMPT / OP_JUMPF case (Ghidra typed the parameter char *; it is the record: *rec == '%' tests op == OP_JUMPT). Branch form from FUN_004137e8: 0 = bt/bf label (0x91/0x90); 2 = bt/s / bf/s label (0x97/0x98); otherwise the inverted branch (form 1: bf/bt, else bf/s / bt/s) over a new label read from the stream, a JUMP record (tmp = rec->tmp, flg 0x10) expanded by expand_jump, and a LABEL record for the new label.

name: expand_move_local
note: OP_MV_LOC case: load (misc & 0x80 clear: ea1 the local, ea2 the register) or store (misc & 0x80: ea1 the register, ea2 the local) of a stack local. Offset from r15 = FUN_0042b20a(local disp, rec->sptravel, 2). Register 0x10..0x1f -> fmov (0xb0), else mov (0x40) of size rec->flg & 3. Forms: offset 0 -> @r15; tmp == 0 and 0 < offset < 16<<size, not FP -> @(disp,r15) (through r0 for a byte/word to a register other than r0); tmp == 0 otherwise -> r0 = offset (mov #imm, or a word/long literal as in expand_call) and @(r0,r15); tmp != 0 -> Rtmp = r15 + offset (mov r15 + add #imm, or literal + add r15) and @Rtmp. Carries rec->flg 0x40 (delay-slot candidate) to the last expanded record.

name: expand_mva_lc_record
note: OP_MVA_LC (0x27) handler of read_next_backend_record (only caller): turns "address of a frame local" into instructions queued in g_expanded_records (count g_expanded_record_count). offset = FUN_0042b20a(rec->ea1->disp, rec->sptravel, 2) (frame offset from the current function's frame record). offset 0: MOV R15,Rn (ea2 moved from rec, rec->ea2 cleared), and when request+0x13d & 4, rec is not a delay-slot record (flg 0x40) and Rn is R0, a NOP after it (both flg |= 0x80). -128..127: MOV R15,Rn; ADD #offset,Rn. Otherwise MOV.W (flg 1, fits 16 bits, g_word_literal_pool) or MOV.L (flg 2, g_long_literal_pool) @(disp,PC),Rn with the offset entered in the literal pool (FUN_0042d8fa find / FUN_0042dc08 add / FUN_004282e6 index; g_literal_pool_label read from the .lit stream by FUN_004137e8 when both pools are empty), then ADD R15,Rn. A delay-slot rec (flg & 0x40) passes 0x40 on to the last queued record. Operands from alloc_ea_operand, records from set_psd_record

name: expand_mva_pc_record
note: OP_MVA_PC (0x28) handler of read_next_backend_record: reads one selector byte from the .lit stream (FUN_004137e8): 0 -> MOVA @(disp,PC),R0 (op 0x44; ea1 = new @(disp,PC) operand, kind 10 base PC 0x6b, with rec->ea1's disp and labels; ea2 moved from rec); 2 -> MOV.W/MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn loading the address from the word/long literal pool (word when no labels and the value fits 16 bits), same literal-pool steps as expand_mva_lc_record; 1 (or other) -> nothing queued (the record goes on unchanged)

name: expand_movi_record
note: OP_MOVI (0x2a) handler: read_next_backend_record, and FUN_00416ff0 (C_JMP), FUN_00418033 (ENTER), FUN_00418df8 (EXIT), expand_fprset_record on psd records they build. Immediate fits 8 bits with no labels, or FUN_0042df28(labels) == 1 -> MOV #imm,Rn (op 0x40, rec->ea1 reused as source); else MOV.W (fits 16 bits, FUN_0042ded3 == 1 or FUN_0042df28 == 2) / MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn from the word/long literal pool (same steps as expand_mva_lc_record). When rec->misc & 0x40 and size (flg & 3) != 2, EXTU Rn,Rn follows (op 0x7c, flg = rec->flg & 3). Delay-slot flag 0x40 moved to the last queued record. shcasm.md's _init_slow_flag probes call it the 0x2a helper

name: expand_movif_record
note: OP_MOVIF (0x2c) handler of read_next_backend_record: loads a float constant. The 32-bit pattern (rec->ea1->disp) goes in the long literal pool; rec->tmp is a scratch register: tmp == R0 -> MOVA @(disp,PC),R0 then FMOV.S @R0,FRn (op 0xb0, ea1 kind 2 @R0); tmp != R0 -> MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rtmp, LDS Rtmp,FPUL (op 0x8d, kind 0xf FPUL 0x67), FSTS FPUL,FRn (op 0xde). Delay-slot flag 0x40 moved to the last queued record

name: expand_mva_fc_record
note: OP_MVA_FC (0x2b) handler of read_next_backend_record: PC-relative (position independent) symbol address. Reads from the .lit stream a 2-byte local label number (big-endian via FUN_0042efb0), a 1-byte placement selector, then (pools empty) the pool label. Queues MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn whose literal is symbol - local label (label_ref labno1 = rec->ea1->labels->labno1, labno2 = -local label, added to the long pool), MOVA @(0,PC),Rtmp referring to the local label (Rtmp = rec->tmp), the LABEL record (op 0x18, label number in the ea1 field) before (selector 0) or after (selector 1) ADD Rtmp,Rn

name: expand_fprset_record
note: OP_FPRSET (0x2e) handler of read_next_backend_record: switches FPU precision. STS FPSCR,Rs (op 0x9d; ea1 kind 0x10 FPSCR 0x68; Rs = rec->ea1->base); MOVI 0x80000 (PR) when rec->flg & 3 == 3 (double) else 0xffe7ffff (clears PR and SZ) into Rt = rec->ea2->base, expanded by expand_movi_record on a local psd; OR Rt,Rs (0x81) or AND Rt,Rs (0x80); LDS Rs,FPSCR (0x8d). Delay-slot flag 0x40 moved to the last queued record. Ghidra split the local psd into local_20[16] + local_10/local_c (its ea1/ea2)

name: expand_extld_record
note: OP_EXTLD (0x30) handler of read_next_backend_record: loads the extended FP bank: FRCHG (0xee, no operands); 16 x FMOV.S @Rn+,FRi (op 0xb0, ea1 kind 4 @Rn+ on rec->ea1->base, ea2 FR0..FR15 = 0x10+i); FRCHG. Delay-slot flag 0x40 moved to the last queued record

name: expand_extst_record
note: OP_EXTST (0x31) handler of read_next_backend_record: stores the extended FP bank: FRCHG; ADD #64,Rn (Rn = rec->ea2->base); 16 x FMOV.S FRi,@-Rn for i = 15..0 (ea2 kind 3); FRCHG. Delay-slot flag 0x40 moved to the last queued record

name: expand_mov_to_r0_with_nop
note: read_next_backend_record calls it for OP_MOV Rm,R0 (both operands kind 1, destination R0) when request+0x13d & 4 and the record is not a delay-slot record: queues MOV Rm,R0 (fresh register operands; expno/filno/linno copied) and a NOP (0x88), both flg |= 0x80 (the same NOP-after-R0-write rule as expand_mva_lc_record)

name: set_psd_record
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void set_psd_record(psd *rec, unsigned char op, unsigned char flg, char misc, char tmp, int sptravel, int expno, short filno, unsigned short linno)
note: fills a backend record's header field by field (+0 op, +1 flg, +2 misc, +3 tmp, +4 sptravel, +8 expno, +0xc filno, +0xe linno); ea1/ea2 untouched. op holds a psd_op (1 byte). 17 callers: the per-op expanders (record g_expanded_records + count*0x18, or a local psd)

name: alloc_ea_operand
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: ea *alloc_ea_operand(unsigned char type, unsigned char base, unsigned char index, int disp, label_ref *labels)
note: FUN_0040cf00(0xc) (size-class allocator), fills +0 type, +1 base (reg), +2 index (reg, 0xff none), +4 disp, +8 labels. Callers pass (1, reg, 0xff, 0, 0) for Rn, (7, 0xff, 0xff, imm, 0) for #imm, (10, 0x6b, 0xff, disp, labels) for @(disp,PC). 16 callers (the expanders). shcasm.md calls it the generic synthetic operand constructor

name: init_debug_info_state
note: run_assembler_passes calls it when request+0x16 (debug information): clears g_line_range_count and g_scope_depth, allocates the two root range nodes (FUN_0040cf00(0x10)) at g_scope_stack[0] and [1] (the second as the first's child +0xc, start 0); when request+4 != 0 opens request+0x80 "rb" as g_debug_variable_input; creates three temp files (FUN_0042f040): g_line_range_temp, g_stack_offset_temp, g_register_map_temp (fatal 0xce4 on failure). emit_final_object_file rewinds/closes the same files

name: update_debug_info_for_record
note: called for every emitted record (and the delay-slot record) by emit_final_asm_record_stream and FUN_00416ff0 when request+0x16. At a label (op 0x18..0x1b) or the record after BF/BT (g_debug_prev_op 0x90/0x91; BT/S and BF/S are remembered as 0x91 so the record after their delay slot counts) a range ends: with request+4, close_debug_scope_range(.., update_register_variable_map()); at an FLABEL (0x1b) the previous function is finished (flush_register_variable_map, free_expno_register_variable_table, two close_debug_scope_range) and g_current_function_label = the label (ea1 field). flush_source_line_ranges(0). Then a range begins: FLABEL -> load_function_register_variable_map + two open_debug_scope_range(0), g_stack_pointer_offset = 0; other labels -> g_stack_pointer_offset recomputed from the function_frame record (-frame size - rec->sptravel - 4*saved regs (FUN_0042ec79) - 4 unless flags 0x8000) and, if changed, (pc, offset) written big-endian to g_stack_offset_temp and counted in frame +0x1c; after a branch -> open_debug_scope_range(1). Then record_source_line_range(rec), track_stack_pointer_offset(rec); with request+4 and rec->expno != 0 counts the expno in g_expno_use_list (descending; 0xc nodes). Updates g_debug_prev_op

name: open_debug_scope_range
note: BBGN handler of emit_final_asm_record_stream (request+0x16), also update_debug_info_for_record: allocates a 0x10 debug_range node (start +0, end +4, next sibling +8, first child +0xc). If the node on top of g_scope_stack has no child it becomes the first child (g_scope_saved_sibling = 0), else it is linked after the child still at g_scope_stack[depth+1] (its +8) and g_scope_saved_sibling = that child. Pushes it (g_scope_depth + 1); start = g_location_counter, - 2 when at_previous_insn (the triggering instruction is already emitted)

name: close_debug_scope_range
note: BEND handler of emit_final_asm_record_stream, also update_debug_info_for_record and emit_final_object_file: when merge_with_previous (update_register_variable_map returned 1, map unchanged) and g_scope_saved_sibling, the node just opened is dropped (saved->next freed with FUN_0040d5cb(.., 0x10)) and the saved sibling is extended instead. Sets the top node's end: g_location_counter (- 2 when at_previous_insn); with request+4 and at_previous_insn 0, if the function symbol's section (+0x1a) differs from g_current_section or the counter is 0, the end of the function's section (FUN_00428140(request, symbol +0x18) -> +0x18 -> +8). Pops (g_scope_depth - 1)

name: load_function_register_variable_map
note: at an FLABEL (update_debug_info_for_record, request+4): reads g_debug_variable_input (host byte order) up to the current function: per function u16 key (symbol id - 0xb6), u16; entries until a u16 variable == 0: u16 variable, u16, u8, u16 n, n x u16 (registers), u16 m, m x (u32 first expno, u32 last expno); then u16. Other functions' records are skipped. For the current function it allocates g_expno_register_variables (FUN_00435550(1, (count+1)*4); count = frame record +0x20, the expno count) and adds an 8-byte register_variable node (next, +4 register, +6 variable) per register of a variable to every expno of its ranges (all expnos 1..count when m == 0), unless that expno already lists the variable. Fatal 0xce6 on read error, 0xbcd on allocation failure

name: free_expno_register_variable_table
note: frees the 8-byte node lists of g_expno_register_variables for expnos 1..count (frame record +0x20 of g_current_function_label's function) and the array (FUN_00435290 = HeapFree), clears the pointer. Callers update_debug_info_for_record (FLABEL), emit_final_object_file

name: update_register_variable_map
note: at the end of a range (update_debug_info_for_record, emit_final_object_file; request+4): for the expnos counted in g_expno_use_list gathers the (register, variable) nodes of g_expno_register_variables into g_register_candidates (0x10 nodes: +4 register, +6 variable, +8 weight = summed use counts, +0xc alternative variable for the same register) and frees the use list; per register keeps the heaviest variable -> g_new_register_variable_map. If a register there holds a different variable in g_register_variable_map: writes the old map to g_register_map_temp (4-byte entries register,variable; then 0xffff), makes the new map current, returns 0. Otherwise merges the new entries into the current map, returns 1 (unchanged). Callers pass the int whole to close_debug_scope_range

name: flush_register_variable_map
note: end of function (update_debug_info_for_record at FLABEL, emit_final_object_file): writes g_register_variable_map to g_register_map_temp (4-byte entries, then 0xffff), frees the nodes and clears it; if the map is empty instead frees the first child (+0xc) of the range node on top of g_scope_stack and clears that link

name: record_source_line_range
note: from update_debug_info_for_record: maintains g_source_line_list (0x18 source_line_range nodes: next, +4 filno, +6 linno, +8 section = g_current_section, +0xa call count, +0xc start, +0x10 end, +0x14 call sites). FLABEL with a line: new node [pc, pc+2] unless it repeats the last. Instruction (op >= 0x40) with a line: extends the matching (filno, linno) node's end to the location counter, or appends a node starting at pc-2 (pc-4 for a delay-slot record, flg 0x40). JSR/BSR/BSRF (0x95/0x93/0x99) add an 8-byte call-site node (pc-2) and count it

name: flush_source_line_ranges
note: writes g_source_line_list to g_line_range_temp: 16 bytes big-endian (FUN_0042efb0 / FUN_0042ef70): filno-1, linno, section, start, end, call count; then each call site (4 bytes); frees nodes (0x18) and call sites (8). flush_all 0 keeps the last node (it can still grow). Counts records in g_line_range_count (fatal 0xc82 at 0xffff). Callers update_debug_info_for_record (0), emit_final_object_file (1)

name: track_stack_pointer_offset
note: from update_debug_info_for_record, for instructions (op >= 0x40): the change of R15 by ADD #imm,R15 / ADD Rm,R15 (value popped from g_sp_adjust_values, which read_next_backend_record fills from the last MOVI) / SUB the same negated / JSR or BSRF with flg & 4 (pops a value, negated); an @R15+ source +4, an @-R15 destination -4. When non-zero, g_stack_pointer_offset += change and while it is <= 0 writes (pc, offset) big-endian to g_stack_offset_temp and increments frame record +0x1c. Functions whose frame flags have 0x4000 and 0x1800 and no record yet only log the pc of MOV R0,R15

name: emit_line_directive_for_record
note: emit_final_asm_record_stream calls it for each record (and the pending delay-slot record before a branch) when request+0x34 == 1 (assembler source output): at a label (0x18..0x1b) or after BF/BT (g_line_directive_prev_op; BT/S, BF/S remembered as 0x91) forgets the remembered lines (free_line_directive_list(0)); then emit_line_directive_if_new(rec); updates g_line_directive_prev_op. Same shape as update_debug_info_for_record's head

name: emit_line_directive_if_new
note: FLABEL, or instruction (op >= 0x40), with a source line (linno != 0): if the (filno, linno) pair is not in g_source_line_list yet, appends a 0x18 node and prints .LINE "file",line via FUN_00426d1d (s__LINE_00441e50; file name from the request+0xec list). An FLABEL whose pair equals the last node is skipped

name: free_line_directive_list
note: frees the 0x18 nodes of g_source_line_list (FUN_0040d5cb(node, 0x18)); free_all 0 keeps the last node. Callers emit_line_directive_for_record (0), run_assembler_passes (1, when request+0x34 == 1)

name: free_ea_operand
note: NULL-safe: frees the operand's label_ref list (8-byte nodes) then the 0xc-byte ea (FUN_0040d5cb). Callers emit_final_asm_record_stream (ea1/ea2 of each printed record and of the delay-slot record), FUN_00416ff0

name: compute_enter_expansion_size
note: OP_ENTER (0x20, case ' ') of the layout passes FUN_004298b6 (pass 0) and FUN_0042aef0 (pass 1); siblings FUN_00421388 (EXIT) and FUN_004216f5 (RETURN). Byte size of the prologue from the function_frame record of the function (label g_layout_function_label_pass0/1 -> symbol +0x10 -> g_function_frame_table): frame flags 0x4000 & 0x1800 add 2/4/6 (a MOVI sized by FUN_00422915; its size cached at item+0xc in pass 0 from FUN_0042e390), + 2 per saved register (FUN_0042ec79), + 2 unless flags 0x8000 (PR save), frame size <= 0x80 -> + 2, else MOVI of -size (cached at item+0xd) + 2. Stores the size in item+5 (char) and adds old - new to g_layout_size_delta_pass0/1. item is a layout record (+4 op, +5 size, +0xc/+0xd cached sizes), not a psd; left int item is the layout_record (+5 size, +0xc/+0xd part sizes) like its relax_* siblings.

name: relax_switch_jump_record
note: item: layout_item (types_proposal.h). op 0x11 C_JMP handler of the size-relaxation passes (FUN_004298b6 calls the handlers with pass 0, FUN_0042aef0 with pass 1, switching on the record's op). Sizes the switch dispatch: an optional MOVI for the case bias (value +0x10 outside -0x7f..0x80, part size +0xc), the MOVI of the bound (+0x14, part +0xe) via relax_movi_record, a JUMPT to the default label (+0x1a) via relax_conditional_jump_record (part +0xf); finds the CTBL record (pass 0: the next record read from g_layout_record_input with FUN_00429c0d; pass 1: item->next) and the table label (+0x18 through FUN_00434510 / FUN_00427a7d); a table distance < 0x8000 means 2-byte entries (pass 1 writes selector byte 1/0 with FUN_004138e9); PIC (request +0x18) adds a generated label (FUN_00416e00(2,..)); pass 1 may create g_literal_pool_label; accounts for the pending literal pools (word/long counts of the pass) and their alignment, clears them (FUN_0042dd9b), stores the pool bytes in +0x1c, updates g_size_reduction_pass0/1, then resize_case_table_record(table, pass, short_entries)

name: resize_case_table_record
signature (C prototype; empty = Ghidra's: void resize_case_table_record(layout_record *table, int pass, int short_entries)
note: table: layout_item (CTBL). Only caller relax_switch_jump_record. Rebases table->offset by the pass's size reduction; when +0x14 (the entry-width flag it last stored) differs from short_entries the table size (+0x10; FUN_0042e390 sizes CTBL as count<<2) is halved and the difference added to the pass's size reduction; stores short_entries in +0x14

name: relax_exit_record
note: op 0x21 EXIT handler (also called by relax_return_record on a built EXIT record). Rebases item->offset; the current function (g_current_function_label_pass0/1 -> FUN_00427a7d -> +0x10 = index into g_function_frame_table, 0x44-byte entries): frame +0 plus +0x24 -> add #imm (< 0x80, 2 bytes) or a MOVI sized by relax_movi_record (part size +0xc); restored registers (FUN_0042ec79) * 2; the flag-word terms are the same formula as FUN_0042e390 case 0x21 (epilogue size); sets item->size, size reduction, then FUN_00428aa3 (literal pool after the record)

name: relax_return_record
note: op 0x22 RETURN handler. Fewer than 2 restored registers (FUN_0042ec79 < 2): an inline epilogue (builds an EXIT record, relax_exit_record); otherwise a JUMP to the shared exit (built JUMP record, flags 2, target +0x14, relax_jump_record); part size in +0xc; sets item->size, size reduction, FUN_00428aa3. Matches FUN_0042e390 case 0x22

name: relax_call_record
note: op 0x23 CALL handler. Rebases offset; displacement from compute_branch_displacement; within -0x1000..0xffe (bsr range): 4 bytes, selector 0; far and not PIC (request +0x1a == 0): 6 bytes, selector 1, a literal of the target via FUN_004281b0 (long unless FUN_0042ded3 is non-zero); far PIC: 6 bytes, selector 2, a generated local label (pass 1 FUN_00416e00(2,..); pass 0 g_pass0_label_counter) and a long literal of the label difference (label_ref labno2 = -label); size reduction. Same body as relax_jump_record without the FUN_00428aa3 call

name: compute_branch_displacement
note: callers relax_call_record, relax_jump_record, relax_conditional_jump_record, relax_mva_pc_record. No label (+0x14 == 0): value - 4. A single label (labno1 > 0xb6, labno2 0) whose symbol (FUN_00427a7d) has kind 1..5 and lies in the current section (g_current_section_pass0/1): target address - item->offset, corrected for the shrinkage not yet applied on that side (forward: minus the pass's size reduction, plus pass 0's for a later section entry; backward in pass 0: plus pass 1's or the section's +0x2c), + value - 4. Anything else: 0x7fffffff (treated as out of range)

name: relax_jump_record
note: op 0x24 JUMP handler (also used on built JUMP records by relax_return_record and relax_conditional_jump_record). The relax_call_record choice (bra range -0x1000..0xffe: 4 bytes, selector 0; far: 6 bytes, selector 1 literal / selector 2 PIC label difference), then FUN_00428aa3 (a literal pool may follow an unconditional jump)

name: relax_conditional_jump_record
note: op 0x25 JUMPT / 0x26 JUMPF handler (also used by relax_switch_jump_record). Displacement within -0x100..0xfe (bt/bf range): 2 bytes, selector 0, or 4 with a delay slot (flags 0x80, selector 2); otherwise the inverted short branch (2/4 bytes, selector 1/3) over a JUMP built from the record (flags 2, offset + 2/4) sized by relax_jump_record (part size +0xc), with a generated label after it in pass 1; size reduction

name: relax_mv_loc_record
note: op 0x27 MV_LOC handler (load/store of a frame location). Frame displacement from FUN_0042b20a(+0x10, +0x14, pass); access kind from attr&3 (operand size), flags 0x80 (other direction), flags 8; displacement class (0 / within 0x10<<size / 8-bit / beyond, second set with flags 0x20); size = byte table 00441978[class*8 + kind] with +2/-2/-4 adjustments (request +0x13d & 4, flags 0x10, attr 0x40 -> -2); far classes add a word/long literal (FUN_004281b0); size reduction. Mirrors FUN_0042e390 case 0x27

name: relax_mva_lc_record
note: op 0x28 MVA_LC handler (address of a frame location). Frame displacement (FUN_0042b20a): 0 -> 2 bytes (4 when request +0x13d & 4 and attr 0x10 without 0x40); within -0x80..0x7f -> 4; else 4 plus a word/long literal (FUN_004281b0); attr 0x40 -> -2; size reduction

name: relax_mva_pc_record
note: op 0x29 MVA_PC handler (PC-relative address). Rebases offset; displacement (compute_branch_displacement) 0..0x3fe: 2 bytes, selector 0; 0x3ff..0x47d while the current size >= 4: 4 bytes, selector 1; else 2 bytes plus a long literal, selector 2; size reduction

name: relax_movi_record
note: op 0x2a MOVI handler, also used on built MOVI records by relax_switch_jump_record, relax_exit_record, relax_fprset_record and FUN_00420670 (ENTER). 2 bytes (4 when attr size B/W and flags 0x40); a constant outside -0x80..0x7f needs a word literal (fits 16 bits) or a long one (FUN_004281b0); a symbolic value: FUN_0042df28 / FUN_0042ded3 decide long, word or none; attr 0x40 -> -2; size reduction

name: relax_movif_record
note: op 0x2c MOVIF handler (float immediate): always a long literal (FUN_004281b0(..,1)); 4 bytes, 6 with attr 0x20; attr 0x40 -> -2; size reduction

name: relax_mva_fc_record
note: op 0x2b MVA_FC handler: 6 bytes; a generated local label (pass 1: FUN_00416e00(2,..) at (offset+6) & ~3, selector byte 1 if offset+6 is 4-aligned else 0; pass 0: g_pass0_label_counter) and a long literal of the label difference (labno2 = -label); size reduction

name: relax_inline_asm_record
note: op 0x10 B_ASM handler (inline assembler block; FUN_0042e390 sizes it (size&1)+size+2 with value +0x10 = size). Rebases offset; in pass 1 adds the alignment padding it no longer needs to g_size_reduction_pass1 (size 0: 2 when the offset is not 4-aligned; else ((size&1)+offset+size+2)&3)

name: relax_fprset_record
note: op 0x2e FPRSET handler: a MOVI of 0x80000 (attr&3 == 3; FPSCR.PR) or 0xffe7ffff (PR and SZ clear) sized by relax_movi_record (part size +0xc), plus 4 bytes (2 with attr 0x40); size reduction

name: relax_unconditional_branch_record
note: ops 0x8e RTE, 0x92 BRA, 0x94 JMP, 0x96 RTS: rebases item->offset by the pass's size reduction and calls FUN_00428aa3, which sizes the literal pool placed after the record (+0x18)

name: list_object_code_byte
note: append_listing_object_code(value, 1, relocatable); callers list_object_code_value, emit_dz_record, emit_dc_record, FUN_00425a51

name: list_object_code_word
note: append_listing_object_code(value, 2, relocatable); FUN_0040d7d0 lists each 16-bit opcode with it when the listing is on (request +6 & 2)

name: list_object_code_long

'>'

note: size_kind 0/1/2: lists the byte/word/long at *value (list_object_code_byte/word/long). Callers emit_dc_record, emit_dz_record, FUN_0041793f, FUN_00417bfa, FUN_00425891, FUN_0042836b, FUN_0042861d

note: builds the section name (FUN_00427d94 with g_current_section_desc and the kind) and copies at most its first 3 characters into the listing line's section column (g_listing_section_field); only caller FUN_00425fbc (section change, object mode, listing on)

name: write_label_name

Callers FUN_0040dd0b, FUN_004262e0, FUN_00427211, ...

note: field 2: offset 0 is written ("0") only when no symbol precedes (after_symbol 0); after a symbol (after_symbol 1) a positive offset gets '+'; callers FUN_0040e072, FUN_0040e5e0, ... pass whether a label list was printed
